name: Exclusivity of Service and Restriction on Dual Employment
text: During the subsistence of employment, the Employee shall devote their whole time, attention, and skill to the business of the Employer and shall not, without the prior written consent of the Employer, engage directly or indirectly in any other trade, business, profession, consultancy, or employment, whether or not for remuneration, that conflicts with the interests of the Employer, interferes with the performance of the Employee's duties, or involves the use or disclosure of the Employer's Confidential Information. This restriction shall not prevent the Employee from holding passive investments or undertaking activities that have been disclosed to and approved by the Employer in writing. Any breach of this clause shall constitute misconduct and may attract disciplinary action including termination.

legal_basis.note: A restriction operating during employment, not after it, is valid and not a restraint of trade
Conduct and discipline as conditions of service, where standing orders apply

invalid_if: Restriction purports to operate after termination of employment
source: Indian Contract Act, 1872; Industrial Relations Code, 2020
title: Exclusivity of Service
authoring_note: LABOUR CODES, 21 NOVEMBER 2025. The four labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025, repealing the 29 central labour statutes this clause previously cited. Section 27 of the Contract Act is untouched by the Codes and remains the operative authority for this clause.
